  A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1A)          i) Write the physical significance of Gauss law in electricity and magnetism.  
  ii) Explain the working principle of Michelson's interferometer with a diagram.             (5)  
  
  1B)          Light from an argon laser strikes a diffraction grating that has 5310 grooves per  
  centimeter. The central and first-order principal maxima are separated by 0.488 m on a      (3)  
  wall 1.72 m from the grating. Determine the wavelength of the laser light.  
  
  1C)          Sketch probability density curves for the lowest energy state of the particle in an infinite  
  potential well and finite potential well.                                                    (2)  
  
  2A)          Obtain the expression for energy density of radiation in terms of Einstein Coefficients.  
  Compare it with Planck's radiation equation and hence show that the probability of          (5)  
  induced absorption is equal to probability of stimulated emission.  
  
  2B)          A glass clads with core glass of refractive index 1.5 and cladding is doped to give a  
  fractional refractive index change of 0.0005. Determine (a) the refractive index of the     (3)  
  cladding (b) the critical angle (c) the numerical aperture.  
  
  2C)          For copper at 300 K, calculate the probability that a state with an energy equal to 99.0%  
  of the Fermi energy is occupied. Fermi energy of copper is 7.05 eV.                       (2)  
  
  3A)          Using the appropriate diagram, derive the expression for the wavelength [Compton] shift  
  for electromagnetic radiation such as X-rays, interacting with a free or nearly free    (5)  
  electron.  
  
  3B)          The stopping potential for photoelectrons released from a metal is 1.48 V larger than in  
  another metal. If the threshold frequency for the first metal is 40.0 % smaller than the    (3)  
  second metal, determine the work function for each metal.  
  
  3C)          An FM radio transmitter has a power output of 150 kW and operates at a frequency of  
  99.7 MHz. How many photons per second does the transmitter emit?                            (2)
